←Module 1
Lesson · 18 min

Navigating the Institution

Who to ask, what the offices do, and how to get a problem solved without being sent in a circle.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Identify which office handles which kind of problem
  • ✓Describe what an academic advisor does and when to see one
  • ✓Explain what disability services provide and how accommodations work
  • ✓Ask for help in a way that gets a useful answer
📘 Reading Lesson

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

The offices, and what each one actually does

On the job

Your financial aid has not arrived and you cannot register.

You call the registrar, who sends you to financial aid, who says the hold is academic, who sends you to advising, who sends you back to the registrar. Two hours gone. The problem is real, and so is the fact that nobody told you which door it was behind.

Your task: Learn the map, so you start at the right office.

Disability services are worth understanding before you need them. Accommodations — extra time, a quiet testing room, note-taking support — require documentation and are arranged in advance, not retroactively. A student who discovers this the week of finals has lost the term's accommodations. If you have any condition that affects reading, attention, testing, or attendance, start that conversation in week one.

One habit makes every office easier to deal with: write down who you spoke to, when, and what they said. When you are sent in a circle, that record is what breaks it — 'I spoke to Marcus in financial aid on the 14th and he said the hold was academic' moves a conversation forward in a way that 'someone told me' does not.

Check your understanding

You have a documented condition and want extra time on exams. When should you contact disability services?

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Find the real answers for the institution you are attending or applying to.

  1. Find and record the location, hours, and contact for advising, the registrar, financial aid, disability services, and tutoring.
  2. Find the add/drop deadline and the withdrawal deadline for the current term. Note the difference between them.
  3. Find out what documentation disability services requires and how long processing takes.
  4. Write the email you would send to an instructor about missing a class for a genuine reason. Keep it to four sentences, and state what you will do about the missed work.
